findings.description: The shared statistics dict on the wrapper is now cleared and reused on every call, and each call's copy writes into this same dict. Concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function therefore share and corrupt each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same @retry function runs in several threads or asyncio tasks, or recursively. Mechanism: stats.clear() wipes the in-progress counters of other calls, and all copies write attempt_number and similar keys into the one dict. Impact: statistics are wrong and unreliable. The old code gave each call its own copy, as the comment above says it intended.

findings.description: The async wrapper's shared statistics dict is cleared on each call and shared between concurrent invocations.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather runs several calls of the same @retry async function. Mechanism: each call clears the dict and the copies write into the same one, so counters interleave. Impact: statistics are corrupted, and a call that has already started loses its counters.
